third, garments discarded by riversides; fourth, garments worn by ants; and fifth, tattered garments. Furthermore, there are another five kinds."
1. Garments burned by fire; 2. Garments soaked by water; 3. Garments gnawed by rats; 4. Garments chewed by oxen; 5.
Garments discarded by a wet-nurse.
Formerly, when Chan Master Wuye of Fenyang was once asked by a monk: "The twelve divisions of the teachings have flowed here..."
As for those who have attained the fruits of the Way, they are not merely one or two.

Why then did the Patriarch come from the West to separately proclaim the Mysteries of the Ultimate, pointing directly at the human mind to see one's nature and become a Buddha? This is simply because the eminent monks of former generations were all thoroughly versed in the nine schools of thought.
"Those such as Daosheng, Sengzhao, Daorong, and Sengrui were profoundly enlightened in the Tripitaka; how could they not have known the Buddha-dharma? The Master said:
"The Buddhas have never appeared in the world, nor have they bestowed a single dharma upon anyone. They merely administer remedies according to the illness;
thus there are the twelve divisions of the teachings. It is like exchanging honeyed fruit for bitter gourds—to wash away the karmic roots of you all."
There is no substantial reality. Through supernatural transformations and hundreds of thousands of gates of samādhi, one transforms those celestial Māras and non-Buddhists.
The dual adornments of merit and wisdom are intended to shatter the views of those who cling to existence and stagnate in emptiness.

If one does not realize the Way and the intent of the Patriarchs, what does it matter if one discusses [the works of] Daosheng, Sengzhao, Tanyun, or Zhiyi? Nowadays, those in the world who claim to understand Chan and the Way are as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
Numerous are those who speak of the Buddha and speak of the mind; though numbering in the hundreds of thousands of billions, they do not remove even a speck of dust from their hearts.

Failing to escape the cycle of transmigration, they never cease their obsessive thoughts, and thus all fall into ruin. Such as these do not yet understand the law of karma and its fruits, yet they falsely claim to be those of the highest spiritual stream.
Like other former worthies, he merely says that whatever meets the eye is nothing but the work of the Buddha, and every step taken is a site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*).
Yet, when examining his actual practice, he is not even equal to a single ordinary person who observes the five precepts and the ten wholesome paths of action;

when observing his speech, he disparages those of the Two Vehicles and the Bodhisattvas of the Ten Stages. Furthermore, while the supreme flavor of *amṛta* (clarified butter) is a rare treasure of the world, he encounters such people as these.
It is turned into a poisonous drug. Even Nanshan did not permit calling it the Mahāyāna;

yet those who merely parrot words compete for the upper hand within the space between their lips, drumming up arguments on matters lacking any foundation. Compared to these people, the other former masters were truly sincere—how bitter it is!
In the *Mahāsannipāta Daśacakrakṣitigarbha-sūtra*, the "Chapter on Relying on Practice" states:

"Good son, there are sentient beings who have not yet applied diligent effort or engaged in formal cultivation regarding the vehicle of the śrāvakas or the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas. Such sentient beings..."
Their faculties are not yet mature; their faculties are inferior; their diligence is slight.

If one were to preach the subtle, profound, and sublime Mahāyāna True Dharma to such as these, both the speaker and the listener would incur great transgressions, and it would also constitute a violation of all the Buddhas.
Why is this? Such beings are in truth deluded, yet they consider themselves wise; they are... [fallen].

They hold to the extreme of annihilationism and fall into deranged conceptions. Clinging to theories of causality, they conceive of the results of all karmic actions as being subject to total extinction.
They repudiate all that is well-done and ill-done, falsely professing the Mahāyāna, and bringing disorder to my Dharma.

They proclaim what is not the Dharma to be the Dharma, and what is the Dharma to be not the Dharma. Those who are not truly śramaṇas claim to be śramaṇas, while those who are truly śramaṇas they claim are not.

"O Śramaṇa! That which is truly not the Vinaya you claim to be the Vinaya, and that which is truly the Vinaya you claim is not the Vinaya—this is due to your foolishness, perversion, arrogance, jealousy, and partisan spirit regarding the Mahāyāna Dharma."

They praise and protect [the teachings], causing them to spread widely. Yet, regarding the vehicle of the Śrāvakas and the vehicle of the Pratyekabuddhas, they slander and obstruct them, not allowing them to circulate.
They are unable to truly renounce worldly life for the sake of the three vehicles, go forth from home, and receive full ordination to become bhikṣus.
Furthermore, they do not truly cultivate and accumulate all wholesome dharmas; such are the causes and conditions.
This is so. Those nihilists who deny all cause and effect, though they dwell among human beings, are in truth rākṣasas.
In future ages, throughout incalculable great kalpas, it will be difficult for them to obtain a human body; at the end of their lives, they will certainly be reborn in the Avīci Hell.
There, they will wander and transmigrate through the various realms of suffering, undergoing manifold afflictions that are difficult to rescue from. Thus it is.

These faults all arise from not having first studied the teachings of the Two Vehicles before entering the Mahāyāna. A verse says: "Those who call themselves Mahāyānists out of delusion and pride lack the power of wisdom;
they are still confused regarding the teachings of the Two Vehicles, so how could they understand the Mahāyāna?
Just as one with impaired vision cannot see various forms, so too one who lacks faith cannot understand the Mahāyāna. There is none.

One who forcibly drinks from the rivers and lakes of the Śrāvaka vehicle—how could they ever swallow the great ocean? Without training in the teachings of the two vehicles, how can one study the Mahāyāna?
Only by first having faith in the teachings of the two vehicles can one then believe in the Mahāyāna. To recite the Mahāyāna without faith is empty talk that yields no benefit;
harboring within a truly nihilistic view while falsely claiming to follow the Mahāyāna, such a person fails to guard against the sins of the three karmas and brings ruin upon my Dharma.
The True Dharma. After those people pass away, they will certainly fall into the Avīci Hell.

When Upāli had finished compiling the Vinaya Piṭaka, on the fifteenth day of the seventh month of that same year, he completed the *pravāraṇā* ceremony.

Upāli gave it to Śuklānanda. Śuklānanda gave it to his disciple Siggava. Siggava gave it to his disciple Moggaliputtatissa.
Moggaliputtatissa gave it to his disciple Candavajjī. In this manner, it was transmitted from teacher to teacher.

Phonetic Glossary:
*máng* has the pronunciation *méng*. It means "the people."
*Kēn* (悋) is pronounced *lìn*. It means stinginess or parsimony.
*Luó* (覼) is pronounced *luó*.
*Tí* (荑) has two pronunciations, *tí* and *yí*. These are names for types of grass.
*Jiá* (跲): pronounced with the *jié* (極) and *yè* (葉) finals; *qián* (箝) is an entering tone. It means to stumble or trip; it means to be obstructed. *Pú* (仆):

Now, the *zong* (essence) is the Buddha’s mind; the *lü* (vinaya/discipline) is the Buddha’s conduct; and the *jiao* (teaching/doctrine) is the Buddha’s speech. They are like the body, its form, and its shadow:

to raise one is to possess all three, for none exists in isolation. When the World-Honored One appeared in the world, during his first year at Deer Park, he expounded the teachings to his disciples to clarify the mind, yet he had not yet formulated the vinaya.
Since the teaching that clarifies the mind is itself the vinaya, there were things [in the beginning] that were not yet permitted.

Śāriputra requested that the Vinaya be codified, saying: "It is not appropriate to discuss such matters before a pure assembly, for it would cause people to say that the World-Honored One suspects an honest man of being a thief.
After twelve years, the Vinaya shall be codified according to circumstances, expounding the five sections and seven groups [of offenses].
At the final assembly of the Nirvāṇa, I leave these words as my final charge, enjoining all disciples to rely upon the Prātimokṣa."
As a teacher, he placed primary importance on the Vinaya, taking liberation through practice as his goal so that the mind might be purified; thus he disseminated the teachings. It is said:
"If sentient beings of the末法 (mofa) age desire to achieve the Way, do not allow them to seek awakening, lest it only increase their learning and grow their self-view."
One should simply apply oneself with diligence to subduing the afflictions (*kleśa*). Furthermore, it is said: "For forty-nine years, I have never uttered a single word.

This is because the capacity for the school (*zong*) is itself the teaching on discipline (*lüjiao*); there is no separate teaching on discipline. The capacity for discipline (*lǜ*) is itself the teaching on the school (*zōngjiào*);

there is no separate teaching on the school. The capacity for the teaching (*jiào*) is itself the discipline of the school (*zōnglǜ*); there is no separate discipline of the school. Therefore, it is not a hindrance to emphasize one aspect over another.
The *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-dharmanetra-piṭaka* was entrusted to the Venerable Kāśyapa; the *Vinaya-piṭaka* was entrusted to the Venerable Upāli;
and the *Sūtra-piṭaka* was entrusted to the Venerable Ānanda. Although these were assigned individually, what was entrusted was in fact complete in its entirety.
Thus, Kāśyapa presided over the compilation of the Sthavira school, and Ānanda participated in the assembly of the five hundred elders; both were matters of Vinaya study. It has never been...

He said: "I am devoted exclusively to the teaching (śāstra) and do not concern myself with the Vinaya. When Dharmatrāta first arrived, the Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci translated the teachings while the Vinaya Master [Hui]lǎn expounded the precepts.
Yet, from those who poisoned Dharmatrāta down to the later Vinaya masters and Dharma teachers, there were none who did not slander the vehicle of the school (zōngchéng).
Others consider this to be because they did not clearly understand the school; I, however, consider it to be precisely because they did not clearly understand the Vinaya."
This is the Teaching. When Dharma came from the West, he transmitted the direct pointing alone and took the *Laṅkāvatāra Sūtra* as the seal of the mind;
how could he have ever extinguished the Teaching? Baizhang left the monasteries regulated by the Vinaya to establish separate "congregations" (*conglin*);

though his rules were many, they followed the tracks of the Vinaya root; how could he have ever subverted the Vinaya? Yet those who practice Chan today deride the Teaching as "Tathāgata Chan" and revile the Vinaya as "mere sound."

Regarding the study of learning: they have extinguished the teachings and ruined the discipline, reaching no bounds in their excess. Others consider this to be a failure to clarify the teachings and the discipline;

I consider it rather a failure to clarify the fundamental principle (*zong*). To claim the title of "Master of the Principle" (*zongshi*) while failing to clarify the fundamental principle—what sort of principle is that?

To claim the titles of "Dharma Master" or "Vinaya Master" while failing to clarify the teachings and the discipline—what sort of teachings or discipline is that? The turbulent waves of the three trainings (*sanxue*) have reached their extreme today.

Alas! Were it not for those who shoulder the burden of the Tathāgata and ferry the four classes of beings across [the sea of suffering], rising up to act as a砥柱 (a stabilizing pillar) against the current, the destruction of the Buddha-dharma would have occurred many days ago.
The holy assemblies of the Western Region (India), during their councils of five hundred and seven hundred, truly felt this with deep compassion.
The assembly at Dongzhen was not a hundred, but ten; not ten, but individuals. Summoning five and gathering seven, whom shall I look up to?
My response lies with my elder brother, Daoyi. When speaking of this, we have always wept together. My brother said: "The school is not clear, yet the world honors it;
the Vinaya is daily perishing, yet the world destroys it. That which is not clear does not merit such honor; that which is daily perishing..."
How could I bear to further disparage it? That they disparage it is truly because they do not understand it. If one wishes to remove what is disparaged, one must urgently seek that which is known.

To divide the Vinaya and the Teachings, and to take them as one's primary principles, yet for those principles not to be the true principles of the Tathāgata’s Vinaya and Teachings—those currently in the world who style themselves masters of the Vinaya and Teachings ought to know how to turn back from this. My earnest concern lies herein.
